menu.doc: The native Semu menu the renderer draws over any emulator with a compositor. The supervisor mirrors this list: the same journal drives the drawn selection and the executed action. A row with `when` shows only where that choice offers two or more (placements: a bezel to place; outputs: a system with two pictures, Wii 4:3 and 16:9; restarts: a system where some choice waits for a restart, its outputs, layouts or players); the renderer draws up to thirteen. BEZEL, SHADER, FIT and ASPECT are value rows: confirm or right steps forward, left back. BEZEL and SHADER step this system's own choice through its variants, then off, live and saved as visual.systems.<id>.bezel_variant or shader_variant, never the global switches, which stay the default for systems without their own choice. FIT switches live between the whole bezel and the screen (game) placement, both at a whole-number scale, saved as visual.systems.<id>.placement. ASPECT steps the output at once and saves it for that game only (visual.games.<id>.<game>.output); the game draws it from boot, so it applies at RESTART GAME. CONTROLLER (where a system has several layouts) steps player 1's layout like a value row, live where the emulator switches it; a layout read only at boot (GameCube on Wii) is saved and applies at RESTART GAME. PLAYERS (where the game takes more than one player) opens a page: one row per player with the pad it holds and its layout (confirm moves the player to the next free pad, or none; left and right step its layout), then RESTART GAME and BACK. Pads are dealt at launch, so a pad change applies when the game restarts. RESTART GAME (here, on the players page, in the settings radial and in the centre of the Wii layer) restarts the game once when anything differs from the launch, and otherwise says so and restarts nothing; no other row restarts the game, and a choice that waits for it toasts RESTART TO APPLY. RESET TO DEFAULT asks for a second press, then removes the system's own choices and applies the defaults live; what only a restart applies (an output, a GameCube pad) waits for RESTART GAME. An action's toast is what the renderer shows for a moment after it runs (SEMU_MENU_TOASTS): {slot} is the slot as the emulator numbers it (SLOT 3), empty with one fixed slot; {label} is the chosen value's label, OFF for none; any change shows the action's toast, and a NAME_toast is the toast for one outcome: loading while a shader chain compiles, unavailable where the system has nothing to choose, confirm when Reset needs its second press, pending when the choice is saved and waits for RESTART GAME, done when it acted, unchanged when Restart had nothing to apply. pause_action reaches only emulators whose emulator.json menu.pause is emulator (seen to keep presenting while paused); the others keep running under the menu, and an emulator without a compositor gets no menu.

gamepad_chords.doc: The plain-controller paradigm: hold Select and press a button. Start+Select stays the quit chord. Button names are positions (north is the top face button); pads listed in xpad_layout_ids (vendor:product, * for any product) are xpad-ordered and report their top button as BTN_WEST, so the supervisor swaps BTN_NORTH and BTN_WEST for them: Steam's virtual pad (28de:11ff) and Microsoft pads. A pad Steam virtualises (named in SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_IGNORE_DEVICES) is read only as Steam's copy, as the game reads it, and one chord read from two pads runs once. On the Deck the trackpad radial emits the keyboard chords instead, which reach the supervisor as X raw keys in Game Mode; both paths produce the same actions.

players.sdl_names_doc: What SDL calls a pad its mapping database renames, by vendor:product (lowercase hex), so Dolphin's SDL/<n>/<name> names a real device; any other pad keeps its evdev name. Read from SDL 3 (sdl2-compat 2.32.72, the evdev path) in the podman VM with uinput pads under the kernel drivers' names on 2026-10-04: Microsoft X-Box 360 pad became Xbox 360 Controller, Sony Interactive Entertainment Wireless Controller (054c:0ce6) PS5 Controller, and so on; Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, Logitech Gamepad F310, 8BitDo Pro 2 and the DualSense Edge kept their names. Steam's virtual pads take their names from Steam's slot file instead.
players.doc: Who holds which pad. A launch on Linux takes a roster of the gamepads present (evdev, those SDL is not told to ignore), Steam's virtual pads (steam_pad_prefix N) in slot order and named from the slot file Steam names in steam_slots_variable (SDL_steam_virtual_gamepad.c), other pads after them by event node, unnamed ones as pad_name. Each pad gives pad_index (its place), pad_name, same_name_index (pads before it with that name: Dolphin's SDL/<n>/<name>), sdl_guid (SDL 2.26's GUID with the name CRC: Cemu), same_guid_index, ryujinx_guid (the GUID with its CRC zeroed, as Ryujinx prints it) and same_ryujinx_index (pads before it with that one: all of Steam's). identities are rendered per player from those; player 1 on the first pad keeps device_identities as they are. first and others give player 1 and the other players their seat: player 1 aims the Wii Remote with the pointer and reads the Deck's motion; the others aim with their own right stick. Without a roster (macOS) player 1 holds the default pad and the others none.
